title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Discover the unique rituals and long-standing traditions that define the Carroll College experience in Helena, Montana.

cards.title: The Haunted Fourth Floor
cards.subtitle: A chilling campus legend
cards.notes: Visit the oldest building on campus to hear tales of the boarded-up fourth-floor bathroom, said to be haunted by a student from the 1960s.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing campus ghost story centered on the historic St. Charles Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Charles Hall is the site of reported hauntings, specifically a boarded-up bathroom on the fourth floor following a student accident in 1964.
cards.access_notes: The building is a residence hall; the fourth-floor bathroom remains boarded and inaccessible to the public.

cards.title: The Talking Saints Legacy
cards.subtitle: Decades of forensics excellence
cards.notes: Join or support the nationally-ranked forensics team, which has maintained a championship streak for over 30 consecutive years.
cards.short_summary: Carroll's elite speech and debate team with a storied history of national success.
cards.evidence_claim: The Carroll College Talking Saints have won or shared the Northwest Forensics Conference championship for 36 consecutive years.
cards.access_notes: Students can join the team; public events and showcases are occasionally held on campus.

cards.title: Homecoming Rosary at the Grotto
cards.subtitle: A spiritual gathering for Saints
cards.notes: Gather at the campus grotto during Homecoming weekend for a communal rosary, a tradition uniting students and alumni in prayer.
cards.short_summary: A traditional prayer service held at the campus grotto during Homecoming festivities.
cards.evidence_claim: On Homecoming Saturday, a rosary is held in the grotto for students, faculty, staff, alumni, and friends.
cards.access_notes: The grotto is an outdoor space accessible to the public year-round.

cards.title: Mass of the Holy Spirit
cards.subtitle: Blessing the academic year
cards.notes: Walk from the Campus Center to the Cathedral for this annual Mass, a centuries-old Catholic tradition to start the school year.
cards.short_summary: An annual liturgical tradition where the campus community gathers at the local cathedral.
cards.evidence_claim: The Carroll community gathers at the Cathedral to celebrate the Mass of the Holy Spirit at the beginning of the academic year.
cards.source_title: Mass of the Holy Spirit | Carroll College
cards.access_notes: The event begins with a walk from the Campus Center; the Mass is held at the Cathedral.

cards.title: Softball Weekend
cards.subtitle: A spring intramural highlight
cards.notes: Participate in this massive spring tournament that brings together hundreds of students for competitive and recreational softball.
cards.short_summary: A popular annual spring tradition involving large-scale intramural softball competition.
cards.evidence_claim: Softball Weekend is a popular spring tradition that brings together hundreds of students and dozens of teams.
cards.source_title: Student Life at Carroll | Carroll College
cards.access_notes: Open to all students; spectators can watch the games at the campus fields.

cards.title: Freshman Retreat at Salmon Lake
cards.subtitle: Bonding in the Montana wilderness
cards.notes: Head to Salmon Lake for a weekend of hiking, canoeing, and mountain-top Mass, designed to build community for new students.
cards.short_summary: A signature orientation retreat for first-year students held off-campus at Legendary Lodge.
cards.evidence_claim: The Freshman Retreat takes place at Legendary Lodge on Salmon Lake and includes activities like mountain-top Mass and canoeing.
cards.access_notes: Requires registration; transportation is typically provided from campus.

cards.title: Commencement Honor Song
cards.subtitle: Respecting local heritage
cards.notes: Listen to the Magpie Drummers and Singers perform a Native American Honor Song, a recent but vital addition to the graduation ceremony.
cards.short_summary: A cultural tradition integrated into the annual commencement ceremony to honor graduates.
cards.evidence_claim: Carroll includes a Native American Honor Song at the beginning of the commencement ceremony performed by the Magpie Drummers and Singers.
cards.source_title: Carroll College Graduation Takes Place Saturday, May 9, 2026
cards.access_notes: The ceremony is held outdoors at Nelson Stadium and is open to the public.

cards.title: The 4-Peat Legacy
cards.subtitle: Celebrating football history
cards.notes: Join the community at Nelson Stadium to commemorate the legendary four consecutive NAIA National Championships won from 2002-2005.
cards.short_summary: A recurring celebration of Carroll's historic era of four consecutive national football titles.
cards.evidence_claim: Carroll College hosts events at Nelson Stadium to honor the 20th anniversary of the '4-PEAT SAINTS' National Championship teams.
cards.source_title: Celebrating the 20th Anniversary of the 4-PEAT SAINTS
cards.access_notes: Events are typically held during Homecoming weekend; some require advance registration.

cards.title: All Saints Day Dedication
cards.subtitle: The heart of campus spirit
cards.notes: Visit the chapel on November 1st to commemorate its dedication, a day that brings together the entire Carroll community.
cards.short_summary: An annual observance of the chapel's dedication on the Solemnity of All Saints.
cards.evidence_claim: All Saints Chapel was dedicated on November 1st, the Solemnity of All Saints, and remains a center for campus spiritual life.
cards.access_notes: The chapel is open for daily prayer and scheduled services.

cards.title: The Mount Helena Hike
cards.subtitle: A rite of passage
cards.notes: Climb the trails of Mount Helena, a traditional activity for students to reflect on their journey while overlooking the city and campus.
cards.short_summary: A popular outdoor tradition for students involving hiking the iconic peak adjacent to the city.
cards.evidence_claim: Carroll students explore the beauty of God's creation through hikes on Mount Helena as part of their campus experience.
cards.access_notes: The park is open to the public from sunrise to sunset.
